easy.explanation: The LORD commands His people to speak comfortably to Jerusalem.
easy.q: Whom are the people commanded to comfort?

easy.explanation: The passage says that Jerusalem's warfare is accomplished and her iniquity is pardoned.
easy.q: What is accomplished for Jerusalem?

easy.explanation: Isaiah says, “the glory of the LORD shall be revealed; and all flesh shall see it together.”
easy.q: What shall all flesh see together?

answers: To prepare the way of the LORD
medium.explanation: The voice calls for the way of the LORD to be prepared in the wilderness.
medium.q: Why is a way to be prepared in the wilderness?

answers: Prepare a clear and level way
medium.explanation: The command pictures a highway being prepared for the coming of the LORD.
medium.q: What does “make straight” the highway mean in context?

answers: Obstacles are removed from the way
medium.explanation: The landscape is leveled and made plain so that the LORD's glory may be revealed.
medium.q: How are the valleys, mountains, and rough places changed?

answers: The way is made level and accessible
The people remain in the wilderness
challenge.explanation: The imagery represents the removal of obstacles from the way of redemption.
challenge.q: What does the raising of the valley and lowering of the mountain emphasize?

answers: To announce to all God's people that their God is revealed
To announce a war against the nations
challenge.explanation: The proclamation is meant to make God's appearing known throughout Judah.
challenge.q: Why is the message proclaimed to Jerusalem and the cities of Judah?

answers: Comfort, preparation of the way, and revelation of God's glory
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from comfort to preparing the way and then to the revelation of the LORD's glory.
challenge.q: Which sequence of ideas appears in these verses?

paragraphs.title: Human Transience and the Endurance of God's Word

easy.explanation: The verse says, “All flesh is grass.”
easy.q: To what is all flesh compared?

easy.explanation: The passage compares human goodness to the flower of the field.
easy.q: To what is the goodness of man compared?

easy.explanation: The verse contrasts fading grass and flowers with God's word, which stands forever.
easy.q: What shall stand for ever?

medium.explanation: Isaiah says that the spirit of the LORD blows upon it.
medium.q: What causes the grass and flower to wither and fade?

medium.explanation: To fade means to wither or lose freshness.
medium.q: What does “the flower fadeth” mean?

answers: People pass away, but God's word endures
God's word passes away, but people endure
medium.explanation: Human life is compared with fading grass, while God's word stands forever.
medium.q: What contrast is made between people and God's word?

answers: The difference between transience and permanence
challenge.explanation: The contrast highlights human weakness and the lasting certainty of God's word.
challenge.q: What does the movement from grass to God's word teach?

answers: To emphasize the temporary nature of human life
To announce that the fields will be full
challenge.explanation: The repetition strengthens the contrast between what fades and what remains forever.
challenge.q: Why are the withering grass and fading flower mentioned repeatedly?

answers: To show that even human goodness is temporary
To say that people never do good
challenge.explanation: Even human excellence or goodness is presented as something that does not last.
challenge.q: Why is human goodness included in the comparison with a flower?

paragraphs.title: The Herald and God as Shepherd

easy.explanation: Zion and Jerusalem are described as bringing good tidings.
easy.q: Who is told to bring good tidings?

easy.explanation: She is told to lift up her voice and not be afraid.
easy.q: What is the herald told not to fear?

easy.explanation: The LORD shall feed His flock like a shepherd.
easy.q: To what is the LORD compared in verse 11?

medium.explanation: The message to the cities of Judah is, “Behold your God!”
medium.q: What should the herald say to the cities of Judah?

answers: He comes with recompense and accomplishment
medium.explanation: The LORD comes as a ruler whose reward and work are with Him.
medium.q: What does “his reward is with him” indicate?

answers: As a powerful ruler and a caring shepherd
As a prophet and a student
medium.explanation: He comes with a strong hand, yet He also gathers and carries the lambs.
medium.q: How are two aspects of the LORD's coming presented?

challenge.explanation: The LORD is both a powerful ruler and a gentle shepherd.
challenge.q: What central contrast appears in the description of the LORD?

answers: The lambs and those with young
challenge.explanation: He gathers the lambs, carries them, and gently leads those with young.
challenge.q: For whom is the shepherd's care especially shown?

answers: To announce without fear that God is coming
To announce that the people are abandoned
challenge.explanation: She is commanded to lift up her voice and declare, “Behold your God!”
challenge.q: What is the purpose of the herald's loud proclamation?

easy.explanation: Isaiah asks who has measured the waters in the hollow of His hand.
easy.q: What does the LORD measure in the hollow of His hand?

easy.explanation: The questions emphasize that no counselor can direct or teach the LORD.
easy.q: Who has directed the Spirit of the LORD?

answers: As a drop of a bucket and small dust
easy.explanation: The nations are compared with a drop and dust before the greatness of God.
easy.q: How are the nations counted before the LORD?

answers: The One who governs all things needs no human advice
medium.explanation: God's greatness shows that no person can teach or advise Him.
medium.q: What is the connection between God's measuring creation and His need for counsel?

medium.explanation: The nations are portrayed as insignificant compared with the LORD.
medium.q: What does “a drop of a bucket” signify?

answers: To show that the LORD is their ultimate source
To explain how idols are made
medium.explanation: The passage asks who taught the LORD, showing that all wisdom comes under His authority.
medium.q: Why are spirit, knowledge, and understanding mentioned?

answers: The immeasurable greatness of the Creator
The work of a human craftsman
challenge.explanation: The images magnify God's ability to comprehend and govern all creation.
challenge.q: What does comparing the universe with small measuring tools emphasize?

answers: They have no independent weight before God
They are greater than the Creator
challenge.explanation: The description stresses the nations' complete insignificance compared with the LORD.
challenge.q: What does it mean that the nations are “less than nothing, and vanity”?

answers: No one can equal or instruct the Creator
challenge.explanation: Both questions point to God's uniqueness and absolute independence.
challenge.q: What common idea appears in the questions “Who hath measured?” and “Who hath directed?”

paragraphs.title: God Cannot Be Compared to an Idol

easy.explanation: The passage asks what likeness can be compared with God, implying that none is adequate.
easy.q: To whom can God be likened?

easy.explanation: The workman melts or makes the graven image.
easy.q: Who makes the graven image?

easy.explanation: The goldsmith spreads gold over it and casts silver chains.
easy.q: With what is the image covered or decorated?

answers: An image made or shaped by human work
medium.explanation: The verse describes a man-made image fashioned by a workman.
medium.q: What is a “graven image”?

answers: It is made by human hands
It is greater than the world
medium.explanation: The idol is a created object fashioned and decorated by people.
medium.q: Why can the idol not represent God?

answers: To make an image that will not be moved
To symbolize the Spirit of God
medium.explanation: The chosen wood is prepared so that the image will remain stable.
medium.q: Why does the poor man choose a tree that will not rot?

answers: The LORD created all things, while the idol is made by man
Both were made by a workman
challenge.explanation: The passage contrasts the living Creator with an object produced by human labor.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast between the LORD and the idol?

answers: The idol depends on people and has no independence
The idol is stronger than God
challenge.explanation: Human effort is required to make and stabilize the idol, showing its weakness.
challenge.q: What does the need to secure the idol with human materials suggest?

answers: It shows that the idol is a limited human product
It proves that the idol is alive
It focuses only on the greatness of the craftsman
challenge.explanation: The steps of making the image reveal that it cannot represent the Creator.
challenge.q: Why does the detailed description of idol-making strengthen the warning against comparing it with God?

paragraphs.title: The Creator Rules the Earth and Its Rulers

answers: Upon the circle of the earth
easy.explanation: The verse calls Him the One who sits upon the circle of the earth.
easy.q: Where does the LORD sit?

answers: As a curtain and a tent
easy.explanation: The heavens are spread out like a curtain and a tent.
easy.q: How does the LORD stretch out the heavens?

easy.explanation: He brings out the heavenly host and calls them all by name.
easy.q: Whom does the LORD call by name?

medium.explanation: The LORD makes the princes and judges of the earth as nothing and vanity.
medium.q: What happens to the princes and judges before the LORD?

medium.explanation: The surrounding context identifies the host as the heavenly bodies.
medium.q: What does “their host” refer to in “bringeth out their host by number”?

answers: He created, ordered, and named them
medium.explanation: God brings out the stars by number and calls each one by name.
medium.q: How do the heavens and stars demonstrate God's rule?

answers: Human smallness versus the ordered power of creation
challenge.explanation: People appear as grasshoppers, while the LORD commands the vast heavenly host.
challenge.q: What contrast is emphasized between earth's inhabitants and the host of stars?

answers: None of the stars is missing from God's ordered host
There are no people on earth
challenge.explanation: Every star is present and accounted for under God's command.
challenge.q: What does “not one faileth” mean?

answers: They present Him as Creator of heaven who reduces rulers to nothing
They show Him depending on kings
They compare Him with an idol
challenge.explanation: His authority over creation and earthly princes demonstrates His supreme rule.
challenge.q: How do these verses support the LORD's rule over earthly rulers?

paragraphs.title: Strength for Those Who Hope in God

answers: His way is hidden from the LORD and his judgment is passed over
easy.explanation: Jacob says, “My way is hid from the LORD, and my judgment is passed over.”
easy.q: What does Jacob complain about?

easy.explanation: The LORD gives power to the faint.
easy.q: To whom does the LORD give power?

easy.explanation: Those who wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength.
easy.q: What shall those who wait upon the LORD do?

answers: His understanding is unsearchable and He strengthens the weak
medium.explanation: The passage recalls God's everlasting nature, limitless understanding, and power to strengthen the faint.
medium.q: Why should Israel not conclude that the LORD ignores its suffering?

answers: To give their strength to others
medium.explanation: The phrase describes receiving fresh strength from the LORD.
medium.q: What does “renew their strength” mean?

answers: Even youths grow weary, but those who wait on the LORD are renewed
medium.explanation: The passage says that young people may faint, while those who wait on the LORD renew their strength.
medium.q: What contrast is made between youths and those who wait upon the LORD?

answers: It counters the feeling of abandonment by showing that God's wisdom is unlimited
It agrees that God does not see
It changes the subject to idols
challenge.explanation: God's unsearchable understanding shows that Israel's suffering does not mean He is unaware.
challenge.q: How does the description of God's understanding answer Israel's complaint?

answers: Renewed strength and the ability to continue
challenge.explanation: The eagle image represents renewed ability and endurance.
challenge.q: What does mounting up with wings as eagles symbolize?

answers: Renewed strength, running without weariness, and walking without fainting
Loss of strength, falling, and disappearance
Building an idol with gold and silver
challenge.explanation: Those who wait upon the LORD receive strength to rise, run, and walk without giving up.
challenge.q: Which sequence describes the result of waiting upon the LORD?
